context: US domestic migration flow map with 12 cities, directed curved arrows sized by volume, and nodes sized/colored by net migration (growing vs shrinking)
first_impression: Structurally honest flow map with correct sqrt scaling for both arrow width and node radius, data-driven domains, and clear legend labeling encoding choices.
what_works: Both strokeScale and radiusScale use d3.scaleSqrt with data-driven domains (d3.extent), avoiding hardcoded magic numbers; node color correctly distinguishes net-positive (blue) vs net-negative (red) cities.
what_doesnt: scaleSqrt is appropriate for 2D area encoding but slightly compresses 1D stroke-width perception — scaleLinear would be more truthful for the claimed 'width ∝ volume' relationship; the map projection renders cities in a very tight geographic cluster relative to the large map canvas, making flow arrows visually indistinct.
